---
title: "Set up your agent"
description: "Install Claude Code or Antigravity into your home directory with the workshop image's install-user-tools helper."
---

The workshop image does **not** include a coding agent. Agents update
themselves about once a week, so a copy built into the image would soon be out
of date. Instead the image ships a small helper, `install-user-tools`, that
runs each agent's official installer into your home directory.

## Install

Open a terminal (**File → New → Terminal**) and install the agent you have a
subscription for:

```bash
install-user-tools claude        # Claude Code  -> ~/.local/bin/claude
install-user-tools agy           # Antigravity  -> ~/.local/bin/agy
install-user-tools claude agy    # both
```

`install-user-tools --list` shows what it can install. Then **open a new
terminal**, so it picks up `~/.local/bin`, and check that the agent is there:

```bash
which claude    # or: which agy   -> /home/jovyan/.local/bin/...
```

You install once. Your home directory is kept between sessions and across
image updates, so the agent is still there the next time your server starts.

::: {.callout-note}
## Good to know

- **It installs software, not access.** Nothing here signs you in, and the
  image has no credentials. You sign in with your own account the first time
  you start the agent.
- **Your home directory has a 20 GiB quota.** Claude Code keeps several
  versions (about 230 MB in `~/.local/share/claude`); Antigravity is about
  280 MB. To see what is using space: `du -sh ~/.local ~/.cache`
- **Run it as yourself**, not with `sudo`. It refuses to run as root, because it
  installs into your home.
- **"Command not found" in a new terminal?** Add
  `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to `~/.bashrc`. The helper prints
  this line at the end if `~/.local/bin` is missing from your path.
:::
